properties.displayName: [WEEKLY] Public-Facing App Auth-Bypass to Server-Side Code Execution (web-server process spawning a shell/interpreter)
properties.description:
Detects a web-application or appliance service process (httpd, nginx, php-fpm, w3wp, java/tomcat, node, or VMware vpxd) directly spawning an OS shell, scripting interpreter, or download/recon LOLBin — the universal post-exploitation tell after a pre-auth or auth-bypass flaw is turned into code execution. This matters this fortnight because a cluster of critical public-facing-app bypass and RCE disclosures landed together: vBulletin pre-auth eval() RCE (CVE-2026-61511) now has a public exploit, VMware vCenter auth-bypass + directory-traversal RCE and ESX VM-escape (CVE-2026-59309/59310/47876), plus a wave of GHSA auth-bypass advisories (LightRAG hardcoded DEFAULT_TOKEN_SECRET CVE-2026-61740, Auth.js fail-open GHSA-8fpg-xm3f-6cx3, Budibase cross-origin credential leak GHSA-mqhr-6j6h-74p5, @better-auth/scim provider-id collision GHSA-rjg6-39jm-rgg4) — all sharing the T1190 → code-execution/destructive-action chain. It spans the exploit and execution kill-chain stages: the auth check is defeated (exploit) and the server process is coerced into running attacker code (install/actions). It FIRES when an internet-facing service binary is the parent of an interactive shell or interpreter it never legitimately launches; it does NOT fire on normal application workers, CI/build agents, or admin-initiated maintenance scripts whose parent is a login shell or scheduler rather than the network-facing daemon. Reference IOCs (<c2_domain_list>, <sha256_list>) are substitution slots only — the parent/child process relationship is the durable signal.

Rationale: Every article in the batch is a public-facing auth/authorization defeat whose payoff is server-side execution or destructive action; the one endpoint signal common to the RCE-capable members (vBulletin eval(), VMware vCenter traversal RCE, and any bypass chained to shell/webshell) is the internet-facing service process becoming the parent of a shell/interpreter — a relationship that survives IOC rotation.
properties.query:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("httpd","apache2","nginx","php-fpm","php-cgi","php","w3wp.exe","java","java.exe","node","node.exe","tomcat.exe","vmware-vpxd","vpxd","vmdird")
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","zsh","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","python","python3","perl","ruby","curl","wget","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","whoami","id","uname")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where AccountName !in~ ("system","local service","network service")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, ChildProcess = FileName, ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
